grh_e2135a8b8235579295dd.title: Action -Berry Kroeger
paragraphs: After suffering symptoms he believes are the beginning of a disabling stroke, 52-year-old Christopher Bell secretly gives up his business and attempts to make his death look like a mountaineering accident on a nearly impossible Swiss glacier. At the point of exhaustion he hears another climber in danger and finds strength he thought was gone, rescuing a woman and reaching safety. The woman later tells Bell that she too had intended to die because of an incurable condition and proposes that each keep living for the other's sake. Her physician husband then reveals she is a talented actress, implying the encounter was deliberately arranged to restore Bell's reason to live.

Malone reluctantly joins their honeymoon trip after a magician mysteriously disappears during his act. grh_e2dc8259ab8a30160bf5.title: George Washington Carver
paragraphs: A biographical dramatization traces George Washington Carver from a child born into slavery to the scientist and teacher who transformed agricultural research at Tuskegee Institute. Carver pursues education despite poverty and racism, then accepts Booker T. Washington's invitation to Alabama, where he builds a laboratory from discarded materials and attacks the South's dependence on cotton. His experiments with crops such as peanuts and sweet potatoes create new uses for depleted land and help poor farmers diversify. Framed as a tribute on Abraham Lincoln's birthday, the program presents Carver's life as proof that talent and service are not determined by race.

GRH catalogs [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]]'s "George Washington Carver" for February 8, 1944. The structured record associates the broadcast with [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]]. Credited performers include The Juanita Hall Singers, Fredric March, and Canada Lee. Production credits include director Anton M. Leader, radio adaptor Richard McDonagh, and host Jack Costello.
The surviving audio runs about 30 minutes.
The episode dramatizes [[work|work.words.4fa8fec17d18fdc6|George Washington Carver]]. Source-work credits identify author Rackham Holt and radio adaptor Richard McDonagh.
